newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks dragged down by Dow at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks dragged down by Dow at close.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed earlier gains in late trading to close lower Tuesday as profit-taking snowballed following a downdraft from Wall Street.
"There was profit-taking, and the Dow dragged it down once more at the close. Volume was heavy, foreigners were in the market but trading was mixed," a trader from the Bancomer brokerage said.
The leading IPC share index ended down 8.41 points, or 0.23 percent, at 3,676.76. Volume totalled 120.3 million shares, of which about one-fifth were due to cross trades.
The Dow Jones closed off 4.61 points, or 0.07 percent, at 6,656.08 points after earlier rising more than 100 points.

"We had a cautious session today, the bourse is very susceptible to international markets right now, especially with U.S. Q4 GDP data and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting coming up," an equity analyst said.
Traders said the market had discounted forecast gains in primary interest rates.
A Reuters survey of money market traders showed an average prediction that bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificates) rates would fall 0.53 percentage points to 22.40 percent.

A total of 110 stocks changed hands, of which 49 declined while 38 advanced. Traders noted the presence of stocks that had lagged the market among the leading gainers and financial groups among the decliners.

Shipping line TMM A shares headed the gainers, up 1.85 pesos (24 cents) to 36.40 pesos ($4.66). Traders noted the company said it would pay the government $280 million for part of its share in a recently privatised railroad concession.
Financial groups Multivalores and Serfin headed the decliners, with Multivalores down 6 centavos (1 cent) to 59 centavos (8 cents) and Serfin off 17 centavos (2 cents) to 3.12 pesos (40 cents).
Traders said banks had declined on uncertainty over the effects of new accountancy criteria on balance sheets, particularly on substantial past-due loans portfolios.
